$comment: Shared definitions for the MAINLINE console read model. Prose contract: contracts/README.md. Licensing: common.schema.json.license (REUSE sidecar; JSON admits no comment syntax).
title: MAINLINE console — shared definitions
description: Scalar shapes and closed vocabularies the console's read model reuses. Every enumeration here mirrors a SQL type declared in verticals/mainline/db/migrations or a CHECK constraint quoted in ARCHITECTURE.md §5. Nothing in this file is invented by the console.

uuid.description: RFC 4122 textual UUID, as the read API renders a UUID column.

hex.description: A BYTES column rendered as lowercase hexadecimal, as encode(col,'hex') produces. Even length, because a half byte is not a byte.

sha256_hex.description: Exactly 32 bytes of lowercase hexadecimal. Presence is not verification — the console re-derives digests in a Worker (D6) and this shape says nothing about whether one matched.

commit_id.description: mainline.commit_obj.commit_id, hex-rendered. Never truncated for display in the wire payload; truncation is a rendering decision the console makes visibly.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant. The read API renders every TIMESTAMPTZ in UTC.

counter.description: A projected non-negative counter. Written by a trigger from an authoritative table, never by the inserter (P2).

gate_epoch.description: The subject's gate_epoch. Increments whenever the gate opens; the merge_record composite FK pins it, so an issued subject's epoch physically cannot move (ARCHITECTURE.md §5.5).

subject_kind.description: The two gated subject kinds. There is no third.

virulence_class.description: mainline.virulence_class, migration 0013. Banded exactly once, in clause_blame_closure, and projected everywhere else.

blame_basis.description: mainline.blame_basis, migration 0014. inferred_semantic can never reach state 'active' (constraint inference_never_blocks).

check_origin.description: blocking_check.origin CHECK, ARCHITECTURE.md §5.5. Eight origins, closed.

clause_relation.description: permit_clause.relation CHECK. The change-request side uses cr_relation.

provenance_chip.description: D5: every gate-relevant number is rendered verbatim with a provenance chip. db:column = a column the database wrote; db:constraint = the name of a CHECK/FK the database reported; recomputed = the console re-derived it in a Worker from signed bytes (D6); staged = hand-authored demonstration data with no cluster behind it; derived = computed by the read API from columns it names in statement_refs.

field_provenance.description: Which chip the console must render beside which value. A pointer absent from this list has NO chip and is rendered without one — an unclaimed provenance is better than a comfortable default. It is a LIST rather than an object keyed by pointer so that the generated TypeScript carries no open-ended index signature: the read model is a closed set of named fields, and its type should say so.

statement_ref.description: Where a payload came from, named precisely enough that a reader can run it. `text` is the statement VERBATIM when the bundle carries one; null when the read API declined to disclose it.

sql_path.description: Path inside the evidence bundle to the verbatim round trip (sql/*.txt), when one was captured.

truncation.description: A truncated closure must never be indistinguishable from a complete one (ARCHITECTURE.md §5.4). Every payload that walks ancestry carries this.

cap.description: The ancestor cap in force when the closure was computed (512 in ARCHITECTURE.md §5.4).
